title: Dense-array seismicity analysis infers a buried fault beneath the Three Gorges Reservoir area
summary: A two-phase dense-array catalog processed with the LOC-FLOW machine-learning workflow revealed microseismicity in three zones and shallow (0–6 km) and deep (6–15 km) layers near the northern Xiannvshan Fault Zone. A steeply dipping seismic band is interpreted as a previously hidden western extension of the Tianyangping Fault; the authors also propose fluid-permeable connections between depth layers. The enhanced catalog detects over an order of magnitude more events than the regional network catalog for the same period.
organization: Wuhan University of Technology; Institute of Seismology, China Earthquake Administration; collaborators

evidence.tested: A two-phase dense-array catalog processed with the LOC-FLOW machine-learning workflow revealed microseismicity in three zones and shallow (0–6 km) and deep (6–15 km) layers near the northern Xiannvshan Fault Zone.
evidence.unknown: Verified from the original publisher abstract and publication metadata; full text was inaccessible in this review. The steep band is interpreted as an inferred buried fault, not independently imaged or proven fault geometry. The proposed fluid-permeable connection and dual-mechanism reservoir-modulated seismicity are hypotheses. The catalog increase reflects a dense temporary array plus machine-learning workflow, compared with the regional network catalog.
evidence.ai_role: The study used LOC-FLOW with dense-array observations to detect, locate and relocate microearthquakes for a higher-resolution catalog. The catalog made the three activity zones, depth layers and steep seismic band visible for the authors’ structural interpretation.
